      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override short-circuits busy-time check",
      "body": "In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the day, the function returns true before running the busy.every overlap check. Any calendar busy time or existing booking during the override is ignored, so slots can be offered even though the host is busy. This can cause double bookings, especially for fixed hosts whose availability must block the whole event."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 117,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override validation allows partially overlapping slots",
      "body": "The override exclusion only tests whether the slot ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. It does not test whether the slot starts before the override or ends after it. Therefore a slot that only partially overlaps the override is treated as inside it. For fixed hosts, a slot such as 09:30-10:30 can pass even if the host override is only 10:00-11:00."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working-hours check accepts slots when no working hours cover the day",
      "body": "The new workingHours validation only rejects a slot if it finds a workingHours entry for the slot weekday and the slot is outside that entry. If the host has no workingHours entry for that weekday, or workingHours is empty, find returns undefined and the host is treated as available subject only to busy times. This allows fixed hosts to be booked on days they have no scheduled availability."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Multiple date overrides on the same day make valid slots unavailable",
      "body": "The date override loop marks the slot as outside if it is outside any override on that date. If a user has two overrides on the same day, a slot inside one override is outside the other, causing dateOverrides.find to return true and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. The logic should accept a slot if it is contained in at least one override."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 142,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working-hours end boundary uses slot start time",
      "body": "The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. The check therefore ignores the event duration when validating the end of working hours. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after endTime will pass, potentially offering slots beyond a host's working hours."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 143,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Multiple working-hour intervals are handled incorrectly",
      "body": "workingHours.find returns true when the slot is outside any single working-hours interval. If a user has split working hours, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a valid slot in one interval is outside the other, so the slot is rejected. The code should accept a slot if it fits in at least one interval."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 114,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Dayjs objects are compared with strict equality",
      "body": "The check comparing date.start and date.end uses === between two Dayjs objects. This compares object identity, not timestamp, so it is always false. The intended handling of a zero-length override where start equals end never triggers. Use .isSame() instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 110,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override date matching is not done in UTC",
      "body": "dayjs(date.start).add(...) creates a local-mode Dayjs, while slotStartTime is explicitly UTC. The YYYY MM DD comparison therefore depends on the server's local timezone and can mismatch near date boundaries. The adjusted override times should be constructed in UTC before formatting and comparing."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",
      "line": 219,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Timezone-converted overrides can wrap to another day without handling",
      "body": "After applying the invitee/organizer offset, start and end minutes are derived from hour() and minute(), which wrap at midnight. If the timezone conversion moves an override into the previous or next local day, the code still assigns those minutes to the current invitee day, which can drop the override or place slots on the wrong day. Converted ranges that cross midnight need to be split or filtered by the resulting date."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts",
      "line": 788,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Missing tests for fixed-host round-robin override behavior",
      "body": "The added test only checks a personal event with a different attendee timezone. The PR description says it fixes round-robin events with fixed hosts and date overrides, but there is no test asserting that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots, nor that busy times inside an override remain unavailable. Those regressions are not covered."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Date override short-circuits busy-time check
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the day, the function returns true before running the busy.every overlap check. Any calendar busy time or existing booking during the override is ignored, so slots can be offered even though the host is busy. This can cause double bookings, especially for fixed hosts whose availability must block the whole event.

findings.title: Date override validation allows partially overlapping slots
findings.body: The override exclusion only tests whether the slot ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. It does not test whether the slot starts before the override or ends after it. Therefore a slot that only partially overlaps the override is treated as inside it. For fixed hosts, a slot such as 09:30-10:30 can pass even if the host override is only 10:00-11:00.

findings.title: Working-hours check accepts slots when no working hours cover the day
findings.body: The new workingHours validation only rejects a slot if it finds a workingHours entry for the slot weekday and the slot is outside that entry. If the host has no workingHours entry for that weekday, or workingHours is empty, find returns undefined and the host is treated as available subject only to busy times. This allows fixed hosts to be booked on days they have no scheduled availability.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make valid slots unavailable
findings.body: The date override loop marks the slot as outside if it is outside any override on that date. If a user has two overrides on the same day, a slot inside one override is outside the other, causing dateOverrides.find to return true and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. The logic should accept a slot if it is contained in at least one override.

findings.title: Working-hours end boundary uses slot start time
findings.body: The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. The check therefore ignores the event duration when validating the end of working hours. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after endTime will pass, potentially offering slots beyond a host's working hours.

findings.title: Multiple working-hour intervals are handled incorrectly
findings.body: workingHours.find returns true when the slot is outside any single working-hours interval. If a user has split working hours, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a valid slot in one interval is outside the other, so the slot is rejected. The code should accept a slot if it fits in at least one interval.

findings.title: Dayjs objects are compared with strict equality
findings.body: The check comparing date.start and date.end uses === between two Dayjs objects. This compares object identity, not timestamp, so it is always false. The intended handling of a zero-length override where start equals end never triggers. Use .isSame() instead.

findings.title: Date override date matching is not done in UTC
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) creates a local-mode Dayjs, while slotStartTime is explicitly UTC. The YYYY MM DD comparison therefore depends on the server's local timezone and can mismatch near date boundaries. The adjusted override times should be constructed in UTC before formatting and comparing.

findings.title: Timezone-converted overrides can wrap to another day without handling
findings.body: After applying the invitee/organizer offset, start and end minutes are derived from hour() and minute(), which wrap at midnight. If the timezone conversion moves an override into the previous or next local day, the code still assigns those minutes to the current invitee day, which can drop the override or place slots on the wrong day. Converted ranges that cross midnight need to be split or filtered by the resulting date.

findings.title: Missing tests for fixed-host round-robin override behavior
findings.body: The added test only checks a personal event with a different attendee timezone. The PR description says it fixes round-robin events with fixed hosts and date overrides, but there is no test asserting that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots, nor that busy times inside an override remain unavailable. Those regressions are not covered.
